title: Rapid Characterization of Genetic Parts with Cell-Free Systems
protocol: Add 16 g of tryptone, 10 g of yeast extract, and 5 g of NaCl to 900 mL of deionized water.
Adjust the pH to 7.0 with 5 M NaOH for 2xYT media preparation.
Raise the solution volume to 1 L using deionized water.
Autoclave or filter sterilize the prepared 2xYT media.
Prepare a solution of 14 mM Mg-glutamate, 60 mM K-glutamate, and 5 mM Tris in 2 L of deionized water for S30B buffer preparation.
Use 2 M Tris to adjust the pH to 8.2 for S30B buffer.
Autoclave and store the prepared S30B buffer at 4°C.
Add dithiothreitol (DTT) to a final concentration of 1 mM just before use in S30B buffer.
Streak Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) Rosetta2 cells or other cell line onto an LB agar plate.
Incubate the streaked plate at 37°C for 10-14 hours.
Use a single E. coli colony to inoculate 3 mL of 2xYT medium in a 10 mL culture tube.
Incubate this tube at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm for 8 hours.
Inoculate 50 µL from the 3 mL culture into 50 mL of 2xYT medium in a 500 mL flask.
Incubate the flask at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm for 8 hours.
Use 7.5 mL from the 50 mL culture to inoculate each of four 4 L baffled flasks containing 0.75 L of 2xYT medium.
Incubate the flasks at 37 °C with shaking at 220 rpm until an optical density at 600 nm of 2 to 4 is reached (approximately 3-4 h).
Transfer cells from each flask to a 1 L container and centrifuge at 5,000 x g for 12 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting into a waste container.
Wash each cell pellet with 150 mL of ice-cold S30B buffer by completely resuspending them using a pipette to disrupt the cell mass, then collect cells again by centrifugation at 5,000 x g for 12 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash each cell pellet again in 40 mL of ice-cold S30B buffer by completely resuspending them and disrupting the cell mass using a pipette.
Transfer cells to pre-weighed 50 mL conical tubes and collect cells again by centrifugation at 2,000 x g for 8 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Weigh the wet cell pellets.
Flash-freeze the cell pellets by placing the tubes directly into liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.
Thaw the cell pellets on ice.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 1.4 mL of S30B buffer per 1 g of cell pellet by vortexing.
Lysate cells by French pressure cell at 640 psi at 4 °C.
Collect the lysate in microcentrifuge tubes on ice and add 3 µL of 1 M DTT per 1 mL of lysate immediately after lysis.
Tap the French press release valve with a small metal rod.
Centrifuge the lysate at 30,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Discard the pellet after pipetting the supernatant to a new ice-cold microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant again at 30,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Pipette the resulting supernatant into an ice-cold microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the supernatant in a 37 °C water bath for 1 h.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 15,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the resulting supernatant to an ice-cold microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant again at 15,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the resulting supernatant to an ice-cold microcentrifuge tube.
Distribute the supernatant in 100 μL aliquots into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Flash freeze the supernatant by placing directly into liquid nitrogen.
Store the supernatant at -80 °C.
Prepare the master mix according to Table 1.
Store the prepared master mix on ice.
Aliquot 30 or 40 μL of the master mix into PCR tubes as specified in Table 1.
Add 10 μL of each variable primer at 5 μM to appropriately labeled PCR tubes.
Place the PCR tubes into the thermocycler.
Run a PCR program with initial denaturation at 98 °C for 3 min.
Cycle through 30 cycles, including denaturation at 98 °C for 15 s, annealing at XX °C for 20 s, and extension at 72 °C for YY min.
Conclude with a final extension at 72 °C for 10 min.
Hold the reaction at 4 °C after PCR completion.
Add 1 μL of DpnI restriction enzyme to digest the original template if it is plasmid DNA.
Incubate the reaction at 37 °C for 1 h.
Analyze 5 μL of each PCR product by gel electrophoresis.
Separate the PCR products using a 1% agarose gel at 180 V for 20 min.
Check for the correct band size based on the chosen core sequence and length of parts added.
Purify the linear template using a commercial PCR purification kit or by the preferred PCR cleanup method.
Optimize the PCR conditions if multiple bands are present by gel electrophoresis analysis.
Purify the correct molecular weight bands using a commercial gel extraction kit as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Quantify each DNA template using a spectrophotometer.
Check that the 260 nm/280 nm ratio is approximately 1.8 for DNA template quality assessment.
Separate a portion of the DNA template using a 1% agarose gel at 180 V for 20 min to ensure unwanted bands were removed during purification (optional).
Use purified DNA templates immediately or store them at -20 °C.
Assemble an appropriate expression construct for each protein to be expressed.
Codon-optimize the gene for expression in E. coli.
Insert the gene into a pET-22b expression vector via the preferred plasmid assembly method.
Transform the expression plasmid into BL21(DE3) Rosetta2 expression cells or other appropriate cell line.
Use a single colony to inoculate 3 mL of LB medium in a 10 mL culture tube.
Incubate these tubes at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm overnight.
Inoculate a 2 L flask containing 750 mL of LB medium with 1 mL of the overnight culture.
Incubate these flasks at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm until they reach an OD600 of 0.6-1.0.
Add 0.75 mL of 1 M IPTG in water to each flask.
Incubate the flasks at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm for 4 h.
Centrifuge the contents from each flask at 5,000 x g for 12 min using a 1 L centrifuge bottle.
Discard the supernatant.
Transfer the pellets to a 50 mL conical tube and weigh each pellet.
Flash-freeze the cells in liquid nitrogen and store them at -80 °C or proceed to step 3.2.
Thaw the cell pellets by placing the tubes in room temperature water.
Add 5 mL of lysis buffer per 1 g of the cell pellet and resuspend by vortexing.
Lyse the cells using a sonicator with a 0.16 cm diameter probe in 15 s rounds with 30 s breaks, repeated 10 times.
Separate the cell homogenate so that there is no more than 30 mL per 50 mL conical tube and keep each tube on ice.
Avoid foaming during lysis, keeping the sonicator tip at least 2/3 submerged in the lysate.
Centrifuge the lysate at 15,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Add 1 ml of Ni-NTA resin for each 5 ml of supernatant and divide into portions not exceeding 36 ml per tube.
Incubate the cell lysate/Ni-NTA slurry at 4 °C on a tube rotator at 10 rpm for 1 h.
Load the resin by decanting the slurry into a 2 mL bed volume chromatography column and discard eluant if not needed.
Wash the resin with 10 resin bed volumes of wash buffer.
Collect protein by adding three resin bed volumes of elution buffer to the column.
Concentrate the eluted protein volume to 1.5 ml using a centrifugal concentrator with an appropriate membrane.
Dialyze the protein against 2 L of dialysis buffer at 4 °C for 1 h.
Dialyze the protein again overnight in 2 L of dialysis buffer at 4 °C.
Quantify the protein using its molar extinction coefficient and absorbance at 280 nm.
Analyze protein purity by SDS-PAGE.
Store purified protein at -80 °C.
Prepare the Supplement Mix by following amino acid solution preparation steps.
Prepare the Supplement Mix by following energy solution preparation steps.
Prepare the Supplement Mix by following buffer preparation steps.
Store the prepared Supplement Mix separately or combined at -80°C in aliquots.
Prepare an additive to protect linear DNA from degradation.
If using GamS, prepare via specified steps or obtain from a commercial vendor.
For other approaches, check corresponding literature for guidance.
Alternatively, use a CFPS system that does not require additives.
Prepare T7 polymerase according to the specified preparation steps.
Prepare repressor proteins according to the specified preparation steps.
Calculate the amount of each component required based on Table 2.
Modify concentrations and amounts of components as needed.
Adjust water amount such that final volume of each reaction mixture is 10 µL.
Modify master mix for dispensing other components by acoustic liquid handling.
Thaw all components on ice.
Prepare a master mix by mixing each component as calculated above.
Mix all components thoroughly by pipette.
Chill a 384-well plate on ice.
Distribute the master mix in 9 μL aliquots into each well.
Calculate the amount of repressor protein required for all CFPS reactions.
Thaw the repressor protein on ice.
Distribute the repressor protein into an acoustic liquid handling source plate or appropriate plate.
Include a serial dilution of the purified reporter on the plate to enable comparison with other studies and labs.
Pre-warm the plate reader to 30°C.
Set the plate reader to read at settings appropriate for the reporter used in the core sequence without shaking steps.
Seal the 384-well plate with an impermeable plastic sealable lid to prevent evaporation.
Place the 384-well plate on the plate holder and begin reading.
